## Register {#register}

Seats are limited, and most of the 2026 room is already taken. The [program](program.qmd) has every session if you are still deciding.

::: {.steps}
1. **Download the registration form.** It is a fillable PDF, so you can type straight into it and save it.

   <a class="btn-reg" href="assets/2026-registration-form.pdf" download>Download the registration form (PDF)</a>

2. **Email the form to Sarah E. Drennan** at [sd33@txstate.edu](mailto:sd33@txstate.edu).

3. **Pay the invoice Sarah sends you.** Payment of $695 is due by December 1, 2026, by check or credit card. Mark which one you prefer on the form.
:::

Checks are payable to **Texas State University** and mailed to:

Texas State University - ALERRT Center\
601 University Dr\
San Marcos, TX 78666

## What $695 covers

Your room at TBarM Resort for three nights (December 3, 4, and 5), and all meals from dinner on December 3 through breakfast on December 6. Travel to and from New Braunfels is on you.

Selected presenters attend at no cost: conference fee waived, room and board covered, and travel arranged and paid by the workshop. One presenter per session is covered; co-presenters are welcome at their own cost.

## Getting there

[TBarM Resort](https://www.tbarm.com) sits on the Guadalupe River in New Braunfels, Texas, between San Antonio and Austin in the Hill Country.

San Antonio International (SAT) and Austin-Bergstrom (AUS) are both within about an hour's drive. Rent a car or use rideshare from either. Sessions, meals, and lodging are all on site, so you will not need a car once you arrive. That is part of the design: the conversations that start on the mat keep going at dinner.

## What to bring

Sessions are hands-on, and most include an active participant role. Bring clothes you can move in. Early December in the Hill Country is usually mild, roughly 40s to 60s Fahrenheit, but pack a layer for cool mornings.

There is no live fire. TBarM has no range, so demonstrations use sims, scenarios, and mat work.

## The four days

Arrive Thursday, December 3, in time for dinner. Friday and Saturday are full session days, everyone in the same room. Sunday morning is breakfast, an informal wrap-up, and checkout. The [program](program.qmd) has the running order.

## Questions {#questions}

<details>
<summary>Who is the workshop for?</summary>

People who train law enforcement and tactical professionals, and people who study that training. The room is a deliberate mix: working trainers, tactical practitioners, and training-science researchers, about 60 in total. You do not need to be sworn law enforcement to attend.

</details>

<details>
<summary>What is on the program this year?</summary>

[x]{.session-count .cap} sessions across Friday and Saturday, opening with a keynote from Rob Gray. The [program](program.qmd) has the running order, and each session has its own page with the full description and the presenter's bio.

</details>

<details>
<summary>How do I get a presentation slot?</summary>

Through the annual call for presentations, usually posted in the spring with proposals due in early June. The [presenting page](call-for-presentations.qmd) has the full requirements and a copy of the most recent call. Selected presenters have their conference fee, room, board, and travel covered.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Can I bring a co-presenter?</summary>

Yes. One presenter per session is covered by the workshop; co-presenters are welcome at their own cost.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Do I have to subscribe to a particular training philosophy?</summary>

No. No particular theoretical school is required. What matters is that you can show your method live and explain why you do it that way.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Where do slides, white papers, and readings live?</summary>

On the [resources page](resources/index.qmd).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Will photos from the workshop be available?</summary>

Yes, on the [photos page](photos.qmd) after the workshop.

</details>

Something else? Email [sd33@txstate.edu](mailto:sd33@txstate.edu). Every question about the workshop goes to the same place.
